lesson.title: Several Functions
lesson.driving_question: How can several small functions make the main program easier to follow?
lesson.primary_concept_family: Decomposing a program into several functions with separate responsibilities
lesson.concept_budget: Compose already-taught function forms into three separate responsibilities; no new function syntax is introduced.
misconceptions: Each function should have one clear responsibility.
A returned value must be stored or used by the caller.
The main program coordinates the calls.
lesson.progression_note: Moves from individual function mechanics to decomposition before functions receive 2D data.

primm.prompt: Recall how a parameter receives an argument and how return sends a value back to the caller.
Use choice 1 and value 6. Trace which function definitions are called and the value returned to print().
Run 1/6 and 2/6. Confirm the main program selects a different calculation function for each route.

questions: What separate job is performed by double() and square()?
What happens if choice is compared with the number 1 even though input() returned the string "1"?
What happens if the user enters 3, and why does the else branch call square() for that unexpected choice?
If the choice is 1 and the number is 6, what result appears?

primm.prompt: Change square() into triple(), update menu route 2, and make choice 2 with value 6 display Result: 18.
Add a third function called half(number) that returns number / 2. Add menu route 3 and an invalid-choice message. Test 3 with 5 and x with 5.

Build a measurement helper with separate functions to show a menu, calculate rectangle area, and calculate rectangle perimeter. The main program collects length and width, selects one calculation, and displays a labelled result; include an invalid route.
Repair the missing return, function-call parentheses and mismatched square function name.

blocks.definition: Breaking one program into smaller named responsibilities.
The single clear job performed by a function.
The coordinating statements outside the function definitions.
A decision that calls the function matching the chosen route.
A value sent back and used by the caller.
